title: Too Many Open Files
subtitle: Healthy dependencies become unreachable after hours

brief.narrative: HTTP responses are not closed on an error path. Open socket descriptors climb until accept/connect fail with EMFILE.
symptoms: Linux File Table metrics diverge from the service-level symptom
The problem reproduces only under the triggering workload
Logs contain enough evidence to distinguish cause from consequence
brief.objective: Identify the root cause, select a production-safe fix, and explain the trade-off.

rootCause.question: Which root cause explains all of the evidence?

options.text: A socket/file-descriptor leak exhausted the per-process limit.
options.feedback: Correct. Files, sockets, pipes, and epoll handles consume descriptors. Raising the limit hides a leak and delays failure.

options.text: CPython’s GIL serializes execution of Python bytecode for CPU-bound threads.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Task granularity is too small relative to multiprocessing serialization and IPC overhead.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Blocking I/O ran directly on the event-loop thread.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

fix.question: Which fix is safest for production?

options.text: Use multiprocessing, a native library that releases the GIL, or a separate compute service; benchmark serialization and memory costs.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Batch work into larger chunks, send compact identifiers, use shared memory only with clear ownership, and benchmark end to end.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Use an async client, move blocking calls to a bounded thread pool, set timeouts, and monitor event-loop lag.
options.feedback: This choice does not explain the complete evidence or leaves the underlying correctness/reliability problem intact.

options.text: Close resources with context managers/finally, reuse bounded client pools, expose descriptor metrics, and keep a deliberate ulimit.
